features.name: Create a basic task
steps: Tap + on the main screen
Enter the task edit page
Enter the title
Save
Return to the task list
The new task appears in the current list
Re-enter the task to confirm the title is preserved. A task should also be able to exist independently without a due date, recurrence, or tags.
features.expected: The new task must be genuinely saved and appear in the current list; it can also exist independently without a due date, recurrence, or tags; the title is preserved after exiting and re-entering.

features.name: Task editing and state persistence
steps: Open an existing task
Modify the title, description, or other fields
Save
Return to the list to verify the summary change
Reopen the task to verify the modified fields still exist; the "modification time" is correctly updated while the "creation time" keeps its original value.
features.expected: The modified fields still exist after saving and reopening; the modification time updates while the creation time keeps its original value; the list summary changes with the fields.

features.name: Start date / due date / time
steps: Create a new task
Set the start date and due date
Use shortcut options such as "today / tomorrow / next Sunday / no date" or the calendar to pick a specific date
Set shortcut times such as 09:00, 13:00, 17:00, and 20:00, or a custom time
Save
Tasks enter the corresponding group by date; after clearing the date or time the corresponding state disappears.
features.expected: After saving the date and time the task enters the corresponding group by date; the shortcut options and the calendar selection give consistent results; after clearing the date or time the corresponding state disappears.

features.name: Recurring tasks
steps: Create a task with a due date
Set the recurrence period
Fixed intervals and periods such as daily/weekly/monthly can be configured
Save

After completing the current instance the next period is generated or the due time advances according to the rules; calculating from the due date and from the completion date produce different and correct results; generation stops after the end date or count is reached.
Compute the next time according to the "starts from the due date" or "starts from the completion date" rule
After setting the end date or count, generation stops when the condition is reached.
features.expected: Complete the system selection flow

features.name: Priority
steps: Create a task
Switch between none/low/medium/high priorities
Save
The visual marker/sort result in the list changes with the priority
After changing the priority the list immediately reflects the new state.
features.expected: After saving the priority the list's visual marker and sort results change with it; switching between priorities is correct; the field is preserved after exiting and re-entering.

features.name: List management and task membership
steps: Create or choose a local list
Create a new task and specify the list
Save
Enter that list from the navigation drawer
Show only the tasks belonging to that list and update the count
Drag an image into the central Drop area, or tap to choose a local image, or paste an image from the clipboard
features.expected: The task belongs only to the specified list; the tasks shown and counted in each list match reality; after changing the list both lists' contents and counts update in sync.

features.name: Tag management
steps: Edit the task
Enter/select one or more tags
Save
Tags are displayed as chips on the task
Set the dithering to the lowest to observe the no-dither result
Tapping a tag shows only tasks with that tag
After deleting a tag association the results change in sync.
features.expected: Tags are shown as chips and still exist after saving; the drawer's tag area counts match the actual task counts; tapping a tag shows only tasks with that tag; after removing the association the results change in sync.

features.name: The font size, line spacing, and displayed-fields configuration genuinely affect the list cards; the same task data stays unchanged; the settings persist after a restart.
steps: Create a parent task
Add one or more subtasks
Save
The main list shows subtasks under the parent task
Subtasks can be completed independently
Collapsing the parent task hides its subtasks and expanding restores them
After deleting or adjusting subtasks the parent task's hierarchy stays correct.
features.expected: Subtask hierarchy

features.name: Reminder
steps: Set a due time for the task
Enable the reminder
Configure reminders such as at start, at due time, and before/after due time
Save
A notification is generated at the trigger time; with a repeated reminder configured it reminds again at the specified interval and stops when the count limit is reached or the task is completed.
features.expected: A notification is generated at the set time; repeated reminders trigger at the specified interval; they stop when the count limit is reached or the task is completed; the reminder configuration persists.

features.name: Places and place reminders
steps: Edit the task
Add a place
Save
The place is shown as a task chip and appears in the "places" category of the navigation drawer
Tasks can be filtered by place; when configuring place reminders, arrival or departure trigger conditions are set
The place state stays associated with the task.
features.expected: The place chip is shown and appears under the places category in the drawer; tasks can be filtered by place; the arrival or departure trigger conditions match the settings; the place-task association persists.

features.name: Description and link recognition
steps: Edit the task
Enter a multi-line description
Save
Control the list summary length according to the "show description / show full description" setting

When the description contains recognizable content such as URLs, addresses, or phone numbers, enabling "show links" generates the corresponding clickable links and disabling it restores plain-text display.
features.expected: The description summary length changes with the show-description or show-full-description setting; after enabling show-links, URLs, addresses, and phone numbers become clickable links and disabling it restores plain text; the description content itself is not modified.

features.name: Files and media attachments
steps: Open a task
Tap "add attachment"
Choose the source among "take a photo / record an audio note / choose from the album / pick from storage"
Complete the encoding configuration
Attachments bound to tasks
Save
Reopening the task still shows and gives access to the attachment.
features.expected: Attachments must be bound to the task and genuinely saved; reopening the task still shows and gives access to them; deleting a task handles the attachments consistently.

features.name: Task timer
steps: Open a task
Set the estimated duration
Start the timer

Won small boards show the player's occupation markers while unfinished small boards show local pieces; legal areas and inoperable areas are visually distinguishable; the current operable area matches the actual routing.
The time stops on pause/end
Continue accumulating after starting again
Save and exit the task
The estimated time and accumulated duration stay correct after re-entering.
features.expected: After launching, the elapsed time keeps increasing; it stops on pause or end; starting again continues accumulating; after saving and exiting the estimated time and accumulated duration stay correct.

features.name: Complete transactions in different shops
steps: Create a task
Check to complete
The task enters the completed state and the completion time is recorded
Hide, keep, or move to the bottom according to the list settings

After cancelling, the normal task state is restored; after deleting a task from the edit page the main list, tags, places, and list counts update at the same time; "clear completed items" batch-deletes the completed tasks in the current scope.
features.expected: The area can be browsed normally after completion

features.name: Search tasks
steps: Create several tasks with different titles/descriptions
Tap search
Enter keywords
The results narrow to the matching tasks in real time
Tapping a result opens the task
The search-result state is reasonably preserved on return
Clearing the keyword restores the results.
features.expected: The results narrow to the matching tasks in real time, with both titles and descriptions matching; tapping a result opens the correct task; clearing the keyword restores the full list.

features.name: Custom filter
steps: Open the navigation drawer
Create a new filter in the "filters" area
Add conditions such as due date, priority, title, tags, and list
Multiple conditions can be combined
Save
The new filter appears in the drawer and shows the match count
After modifying a task's attributes the filtered results and counts are recomputed.
features.expected: After saving, the filter appears in the drawer and shows the match count; combined conditions take effect; after task attributes change the filter results and counts are recomputed; deleting a filter does not affect the task data.

features.name: List grouping, sorting, and display controls
steps: Open the list sort panel
Select fields such as the due date for grouping and set ascending/descending
Set the sort field to conditions such as the due date
The main list is reorganized according to the rules; toggle "show unstarted items / show completed tasks / show completed subtasks / move completed tasks to the bottom", etc.
The list responds immediately and the task data itself is not deleted.
features.expected: Grouping and sorting reorganize the list according to the rules with the order genuinely changing; each display toggle only affects visibility without deleting tasks; the settings persist.

features.name: Task-list card content configuration
steps: Enter "task list options"
Adjust the font size and line spacing
Control whether the full title, description, full description, and links are shown
Toggle the elements such as subtasks, start date, place, list, and tags in the "card" area
Return to the task list
The same task's data stays unchanged while the card's displayed fields and layout change accordingly.
features.expected: The field order and visibility change according to the settings

features.name: Custom task
steps: Settings
Edit-screen options
Enter "customize edit screen"
Open "details" on a song
Return to the task edit page
The field order and visibility change according to the settings; hidden fields are no longer shown but their data is not lost; restoring defaults restores the initial layout.
"Restore defaults" restores the initial layout.
features.expected: They enter the current queue

features.name: Defaults and the complete persistence loop
steps: Set "task defaults"
Specify the default list, tags, priority, start date, due date, recurrence, reminders, place, etc.
Create a new task
New tasks automatically inherit these defaults
Manually modify some of the fields and save
Exit the app / reopen
The task itself, the default configuration, the list counts, and the tag and place relationships remain consistent.
features.expected: New tasks automatically inherit the default list, tags, priority, dates, etc.; after manual modification the modified values are saved; after a restart the tasks, default configuration, counts, and tag and place relationships stay consistent.
